title: Why Your To-Do List Isn't the Problem

shots.voiceover: The problem isn't your to-do list. It's that to-do lists were never designed for ADHD brains.
shots.textOverlay: your to-do list is not the problem

shots.voiceover: You've tried every app. Every notebook. Every color-coded system. And at the end of the day, the list is longer than it was this morning.
shots.textOverlay: tried every system. list still growing.

shots.voiceover: Standard to-do lists work on the assumption that seeing a task is enough to start it. For neurotypical brains, that's mostly true. For ADHD brains, seeing the task and initiating the task are two completely different neurological events — separated by a dopamine gap. The list becomes a reminder of everything you haven't done, which spikes cortisol, which tanks motivation, which makes the gap wider.
The fix: replace the list with a box. One task, one time window. When the window closes, you're done — regardless of whether the task is finished. The box removes the infinite-list guilt loop.
That's the BoxDay idea. Link in bio.
